scope: current PSP source adapter against a fresh isolated upstream release
psp_commit_note: base commit of the review branch, cut from origin/main; the adapter change in this branch (isPermanentPanelMsg matching the SS-2022 message) does not alter any endpoint the live suite drives, so the verified adapter surface is this commit plus that classification-only change

environment.platform: linux/arm64 (Lima VM, nerdctl), the same isolated-panel launcher CI uses
environment.authentication: admin-scoped Bearer token, minted through the panel's apiTokens/create

ci_image_architecture: the digest above is the multi-arch manifest list (docker-content-digest), so the amd64 leg CI runs and the arm64 leg run here are the same reviewed release
checker: go tool test2json | deploy/compat/check-go-results.mjs --profiles deploy/compat/profiles-third-party.json --profile third-party-3xui-live

notApplicable.reason: needs a fail2ban endpoint the 3X-UI image does not run; not part of the panel-backed surface

supplementary.method: temporary in-package Go test overlay driving the production adapter (same client construction as the standing TestLive_ suite), not committed

checks.check: SS-2022 aes-128-gcm and aes-256-gcm inbound add + update
SS-2022 chacha20-poly1305 inbound add (with and without a client) and update

answer_envelope.msg: Something went wrong (shadowsocks inbound method 2022-blake3-chacha20-poly1305 does not support multiple users, use a 2022-blake3-aes method)

checks.why_it_is_not_a_capability_loss: On 3.9.0 the panel SAVES this inbound and then xray-core fails to build it — 'shadowsocks 2022 (multi-user): only blake3-aes-*-gcm methods are supported', core exit status 23, xray state=error, the whole core down and no listener, which takes every OTHER inbound down with it. Verified live on a fresh 3.9.0 panel: add chacha20+client → panelVersion 3.9.0 reports xray state 'error' within 10s and 24445 is not listening. So 3.10.0 turns a config that silently kills the core into a save-time refusal. It is not a working configuration PSP loses.
checks.adapter_change: isPermanentPanelMsg now matches 'does not support multiple users', so the write fails fast as domain.ErrValidation instead of burning the sync task's ~100-attempt budget and writing an audit row per attempt

checks.check: Hysteria2 salamander obfs password of 4+ bytes and the omitted-obfs case
Hysteria2 salamander obfs password below 4 bytes ('abc')

answer_envelope.msg: Something went wrong (salamander finalmask password must be at least 4 bytes; xray-core refuses a shorter one)

checks.adapter_change: none needed — the pre-existing 'finalmask' marker already classifies it permanent; pinned by a test case so that marker cannot silently stop covering it

source_review.method: git diff v3.9.0..v3.10.0 over the upstream tree (563+303 files touched across the two releases)
findings: no route added or removed on the /panel/api surface PSP calls; api.go changed only to widen the node-sync scope allowlist (nodeSyncScopeAllow gains /inbounds/:id/subSortIndex, /clients/bulkResetTraffic, /clients/activeInbounds)
model.Client and xray.ClientTraffic are byte-identical between 3.9.0 and 3.10.0

the controller diff is api.go (scope map), inbound.go (MasterPushHeader marks a master-push request as node-sync when the master holds an admin token) and xray_setting.go (+2 lines); none changes a response PSP parses
inbound.go's AddInbound/UpdateInbound gain validateFinalMaskSalamander, validateXDriveStorage and validateShadowsocks2022Inbound — the two PSP-relevant ones are recorded under supplementary above

new boot migrations migrateShadowsocks2022ChachaInbounds (rewrites a stored chacha20 method to aes-256-gcm) and repairShadowsocks2022ServerKeys (replaces an unparseable stored server key); neither touches a method PSP writes (aes-128/aes-256 keep their keys)
normalizeSubSortIndex is unchanged (zero → 1, explicit negatives kept), so the negative-subSortIndex behaviour 3.9.0 verification pinned still holds

limits: fail2ban probes N/A; declared subtests may appear in checker unexpected and do not count as top-level failures
adapter-surface evidence only: no historical PSP binary, no existing-database upgrade, no full proxy dataplane or PSP traffic/reconcile-chain verification
no destructive panel/core update execution (updatePanel / installXray reachability only)
the supplementary SS-2022/salamander probes drove inbound add/update directly through the adapter; they were not run through the full node-create and reconcile push paths
3X-UI 3.10.0's new protocols (MASQUE, XDRIVE) and its native TUIC/AmneziaWG additions are outside PSP's supported feature set and were not exercised
